title: Basic 3 · Pad an image
summary: Grow the canvas around an image with Pad, exploring fill modes (average / set / border / circular).

steps.title: Try padding
steps.body: Pad grows an image by adding a border around it. In cryo-EM it's used routinely before and after Fourier transforms to avoid wrap-around artefacts at the box edges.

steps.title: Drop the data node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · Clock face** (a 128×128 image).

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.clock` shows its image before we add the next stage.

steps.title: Wire Clock → Pad
steps.body: Drag from Clock's `image` output to Pad's `image` input.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. With default sizes the output equals the input — a baseline before you grow the canvas.

steps.title: Click Pad
steps.body: Click Pad. The Inspector reveals `ny` / `nx` (output size), `pad_type` (how to fill the border: average = image mean, set = the `background` value, etc.), and `background`.

steps.title: Set ny to 256
steps.body: Enter **256** in `ny` — doubles the vertical output size.

steps.title: Set nx to 256
steps.body: Enter **256** in `nx` too. Output becomes 256×256 with the original 128×128 clock centred and 64 pixels of fill all around.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. Pad emits a 256×256 image: the clock face in the middle, surrounded by the image's mean value (default `pad_type = average`).

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body: Switch to `pad_type = set` with `background = 0` to pad with zeros (= black). That's the usual pre-processing step before a Fourier filter. Next, **Basic 4 · Apply a mask**.
